chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Saeed, from Aban ibn Taghlub, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The best of my community are those who, when they travel, break their fast and shorten (the prayer); and when they are shown kindness, they rejoice; and when they sin, they seek forgiveness. And the worst of my community are those who are born into blessings, fed with them, eat the best of food, wear soft clothes, and when they speak, they are not truthful.'
ai.seo_question: What are the characteristics of the best and worst members of the Muslim community according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) delineates the spiritual character of the community by contrasting the ascetic piety of travelers—marked by fasting, qasr, and repentance—with the moral decay of those raised in luxury. It highlights that true virtue lies not in material comfort but in adherence to prophetic practices and truthfulness, a key theme in Shia ethical scholarship regarding the balance between worldly ease and spiritual vigilance.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Salih Bin Saeed, from Aban Bin Taghlub, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The best of my<sup>saww</sup> community are those, when they are travelling, they are not Fasting, and they are shortening (the Prayer); and when they are done a favour, they welcome it as a glad tiding, and when they are sinning, they seek Forgiveness. And, the most evil ones of my<sup>saww</sup> community are those who are born among the Bounties, and they are fed with it, consuming the best of the foods, and they are wearing soft clothes, and when they are speaking, they are not truthful’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Salih ibn Sa‘id from Aban ibn Taghlib who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has stated this Hadith: ‘The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, “The virtuous among my followers are those who, when on a journey, stop fasting and reduce their Salat (prayer), when receiving a favor they take it as good news and when doing a sin ask for forgiveness. The evildoers among my followers are those who are born in bounties and feed on it, who eat fine food, wear soft clothes and when speaking do not tell the truth.’””
